task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-11-01, in the area of player absence and offensive reorganization):
How much the offense reorganizes (relative to L) predicts the change in points per possession.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): n=986; n=148, mde rho; 148 spells

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

historical_evidence.finding: Earlier suppression triggers leave time to act and yield better BEST-counter outcomes; Spearman rho -0.2066 p=1e-06 n=557; BEST-AVOID gap early 0.701 vs late 0.415.
Real player absences move the association structure (V1) and the LOO simulation predicts the magnitude (V2). V1(a) 16/23 above p95 binomial p=2.67e-16; V2a rho=+0.288 p=0.077.
Player routing V4 vs V5 direct scoring; 8 divergences, 0 scoreable, 8 unscored.
Routing prior vs H2H posterior gate diagnostic; apparent +1.13 PPP [source] is small-sample inflation.

failed_approaches.why: A_unanswerable (question not answerable with the data or design) and [prior work]

failed_approaches.what_failed: Small-sample distortion in routing gate analysis
failed_approaches.why: C_artifact (apparent effect produced by a construction, selection or labelling flaw) and [prior work]

evidence_does_not_establish: No prior study directly addressed the relationship between offense reorganization relative to L and change in points per possession; existing studies faced small sample, untestability, or artifacts.
own_inferences: The metric of offense reorganization relative to L is not defined in the available data; likely requires complex graph-based construction; the sample of 148 spells may be insufficient for robust predictive modeling; confounding by game context (opponent strength, home/away, score differential) is likely.
uncertainties: Whether the offense reorganization metric can be reliably computed from the play-by-play; whether the 148 spells provide enough variation in reorganization magnitude; potential unmeasured confounders.

historical_effect.explanation: The retrieved records did not directly address the proposed question, so they do not alter the decision to proceed or not.

blocking_constraints.text: Only 148 spells available, limiting power for detecting moderate effect sizes.
Player absences and associated reorganization events are relatively rare.
Offense reorganization metric relative to L is not yet validated.
Game context and opponent factors may confound the association.

prior_work.summary: No prior study has directly examined how offense reorganization relative to L predicts changes in points per possession.

risks.text: Limited number of spells reduces statistical power.
Rare occurrence of player absences limits exposure variability.
Potential confounders such as opponent defense and game situation.

design.estimand: Association between magnitude of offense reorganization (relative to L) and change in points per possession during player absence spells.
design.unit: Game-level reorganization magnitude and possession-level PPP change.
design.sample: All player absence spells (n≈148) across NBA 2022‑26 seasons.
design.power: Estimated to detect a Spearman rho of 0.3 with 80% power would require >400 spells; current sample insufficient.
design.controls: Baseline PPP, opponent defensive rating, home/away, score differential, game phase.
design.falsification: Test the same model on non‑absence periods to check for spurious association.
design.multiplicity: Apply Bonferroni correction for multiple reorganization metrics if more than one is tested.
design.decision_rule: Reject null if p<0.05 after correction; otherwise conclude insufficient evidence.
design.data_version: NBA 2025‑26 season data up to 2026‑04‑13 (full regular season) and 2026‑06‑21 (full playoffs).
